Impossibility is proved over all F_t-adapted u, and feasibility uses u=0, which needs no information. Both therefore hold for every intermediate information pattern."},{"id":"L1a","claim":"Transition Phi, pathwise variation of constants, well-posedness for N1 inputs","status":"verified","note":"Set x=Y c with Y=Phi(.,0) and c=int Y^{-1} w(.-h). c has bounded variation, so d[Y,c]=0 and dx=(ax+w(t-h))dt+sigma x dW. N1(w) finite gives int_0^L w^2 finite a.s., so the forcing is pathwise L1. Uniqueness follows from the homogeneous linear SDE."},{"id":"L1b","claim":"Pathwise Minkowski, then Tonelli, and independence of R_s from w(s)","status":"verified","note":"Pathwise, ||x||_{L2[0,T]}<=int_0^L |w(s)| R_s ds. This is legitimate because w enters only the drift, so the representation is a Lebesgue integral and no stochastic-integral Minkowski is needed. R_s depends only on increments after s+h, so it is independent of F_{s+h}, which contains w(s). The product rule for nonnegative variables holds even if E|w(s)| is infinite. The step needs only w(s) in F_{s+h}, and it fails for anticipating w, as the text says."},{"id":"L1c","claim":"M=E||G||_{L2(0,inf)}<=H_delta using only a<0","status":"verified","note":"Cocycle G(n delta+rho)=G(n delta)G_n(rho) with G_n an independent copy. E G(r)=e^{ar}. Jensen is applied on each block, then the geometric sum. q<0 is not needed. The last step, E int|w|<=sqrt(L) N1(w), is pathwise Cauchy-Schwarz."},{"id":"H","claim":"Hilbert estimate N2(Su)<=M_T N2(u), with M_T^2=(e^{qT}-1-qT)/q^2, or T^2/2 when q=0","status":"verified","note":"It is correctly labelled as an upper bound only. It requires u(s) to be F_s-measurable and B0=0."},{"id":"L2-data","claim":"q=2; u=-2x gives 2(A-2B)+A0^2=-2; D1'D1=1e4; D1'D0=0","status":"verified","note":""},{"id":"L2.1","claim":"Literal gain of u=0 is at most 2H_1, which is below 6, for all adapted and N1 inputs (L4); certificate 168/5<36","status":"verified","note":"2H_1 is about 5.655 (square about 31.98). The 8/3<e<11/4 certificate is correct and each bound is used in the right direction."},{"id":"L2.2a","claim":"Pulse moments m, s and the constant D (L5)","status":"verified","note":"m=1-e^{-r} and s=e^{2r}/3-1+(2/3)e^{-r}, so s(1) is about 1.70827 and D is about 343.73. Dropping int_0^1 s (about 0.486) gives a valid lower bound."},{"id":"L2.2b","claim":"All-controller mean-square lower bound (L6) exceeds 14","status":"verified by hand; not by the unrun verifier","note":"x=d+Su holds for any adapted u, including nonlinear rules, because B0=0 and the plant is linear. S acts on all of [0,5], so control applied before the pulse arrives is included. The test input is deterministic, so the controller may know w completely at time 0. N2(z) finite forces u into L2. The triangle inequality and 2D Cauchy-Schwarz steps are correct. The value is about 14.890."},{"id":"L2-sep","claim":"Existence separation at gamma=6, for deterministic and for adapted disturbances","status":"verified","note":"Literal problem: a feasible controller exists (u=0). Mean-square problem: no F_t-adapted controller is feasible, shown with one deterministic input that is admissible in both classes. This is a genuine existence separation, not a comparison for one controller or one input law."},{"id":"L2-Ric","claim":"Refutes necessity of the mean-square Riccati condition for the literal finite-horizon problem","status":"conditional","note":"Relies on unpinned old theorems; see findings."},{"id":"L3a","claim":"Pointwise completion |z|^2=(dx)^2/2+2(u+dx/2)^2 makes u* pathwise optimal over all controllers","status":"verified","note":"This works because B=B0=0, so x does not depend on u. It covers nonlinear, history-dependent and randomized controllers, and any norm that is monotone in |z|."},{"id":"L3b","claim":"Optimal literal gain is exactly 1 for adapted and deterministic inputs, on the N1 and square-integrable input spaces; strictly feasible iff gamma>1","status":"verified","note":"Sufficiency: u* gives N1(z)<=N1(w), using E(G|X|)=E|X| (X is F_1-measurable and G is independent of F_1); V may depend on G. Necessity: the deterministic input with X=V=1 gives ratio exactly 1 under u*, hence at least 1 for every controller."},{"id":"L3c","claim":"Optimal mean-square gains: adapted sqrt((1+e)/2), deterministic sqrt((e+1+sqrt((e-1)^2+4))/4)","status":"verified","note":"The adapted extremal input w=G/e on [2,3] is F_2-measurable, and both equality conditions hold. The values are about 1.3635 and 1.2605, and the text keeps them distinct."},{"id":"Hor","claim":"Only finite horizons are asserted; u=0 is not mean-square stable on the infinite horizon","status":"verified","note":"q=2>0. No infinite-horizon conclusion is drawn, and the horizon paragraph is appropriately hedged."}],"findings":[{"severity":"minor (proof completeness; the claim itself is true)","section":"Theorem L2, proof of 2, inequality (L6)","problem":"The strict inequality sqrt(D/(1+(e^10-11)/40000))>14 is justified in the text only by Fraction arithmetic 'in the verifier', and that verifier has not run. As written, this load-bearing step has no in-text proof, unlike (L4). Independently, the inequality holds with a wide margin: ratio^2 is about 221.7 against 196, so the gain is about 14.890.","suggested_fix":"Add an inline certificate. D is increasing in e because d s(1)/de=2(e^3-1)/(3e^2)>0, and the denominator is also increasing in e. Using 27/10<e<68/25 (from partial sums 65/24<e<2.7183): D>(13583/8100)(2.7^6-1)/2, about 323.997, and the denominator is below 1+(2.72^10-11)/40000, about 1.55388. Then ratio^2>208.5>196, so the gain exceeds 14.43. Keep the verifier as a pending cross-check."},{"severity":"minor (unpinned dependency)","section":"Theorem L2 closing paragraph; Section 4 'Old mean-square Theorems 1--2'","problem":"Refuting necessity of the Riccati condition requires showing that the Riccati condition fails at gamma=6. The pinned proof shows only mean-square infeasibility at 6. Going from that to failure of the Riccati condition uses the sufficiency half of the old theorems (Riccati(gamma) implies mean-square feasibility), which are not in this file. It also requires those theorems to be stated for the same horizon [0,5], information pattern and disturbance class.","suggested_fix":"State the self-contained result: literal feasibility at gamma does not imply mean-square feasibility at gamma. Then give the Riccati corollary explicitly conditioned on that old sufficiency result, naming its horizon, input class and information pattern."},{"severity":"exposition","section":"Theorem L2, statement 2","problem":"'Allowed the whole Brownian filtration' can be read as giving the controller the entire Brownian path in advance. The Hilbert-estimate independence step requires u(s) to be F_s-measurable and fails for anticipating controls. Section 0 states the correct class.","suggested_fix":"Replace with 'any (F_t)-adapted, nonanticipative control (full past history, independent randomization, and complete knowledge of the deterministic test input allowed)'."},{"severity":"exposition (scope wording)","section":"Header, Section 3 title, Theorem L3, Section 4 'N&S benchmark'","problem":"'Subclass' and 'class' suggest a family of systems, but L3 treats one fixed plant (unit gates, unit noise, fixed weights). The N&S result is genuine for that plant. However, because B=B0=0 and h=0, synthesis reduces to pointwise output cancellation. The plant therefore tests neither preview information nor state actuation.","suggested_fix":"Call it a 'single gated benchmark plant', or parameterize the gates and noise and prove the result for that family. Add one sentence saying it tests neither preview nor actuation."},{"severity":"exposition","section":"Section 0 last paragraph; Theorem L3","problem":"u*(t)=-d(t)x(t)/2 is time-varying. It matches the book's form u=F(x(t),w|[t-h,t]) only if F may depend on t. That is natural here, since the plant itself is time-varying and outside the book's class.","suggested_fix":"Describe it as 'time-varying memoryless state feedback with the book's information pattern (h=0)'."},{"severity":"exposition","section":"Theorem L2, proof of 2","problem":"The symbol M is used twice. In L1, M=E||G||_{L2(0,inf)}. In the L2 proof, M^2=(e^10-11)/4 is the Hilbert constant M_T at T=5.","suggested_fix":"Write M_5 in the L2 proof."},{"severity":"exposition (evidence labeling)","section":"Header; Section 4 'Evidence labels' and reproduction block","problem":"The text presents 'new evidence', 'exact arithmetic and independent moment-ODE countercheck' and a retained other-vendor referee result as already existing. No verifier has run, so these are planned checks, not evidence.","suggested_fix":"Mark them as pending until the run artifacts exist. Once the (L6) gap is fixed, the analytic proofs do not depend on them."},{"severity":"optional (sharpening/robustness)","section":"Theorem L2, proof of 1","problem":"delta=1 is not optimal. H_delta is smallest near delta=0.48, about 2.355 (H_{1/2} is about 2.356), which gives literal gain at most 4.71 instead of 5.66. This also removes a convention risk: if the book counted an input interval of length 5 (for example a preview segment w on [-1,0) entering on [0,1]), delta=1 would give sqrt(5)H_1, about 6.32, which exceeds 6, while delta=1/2 gives about 5.27.","suggested_fix":"Optionally use delta=1/2 with the certificate e<11/4 and e^{1/2}>79/48. Then L((e-1)/2)/(1-e^{-1/2})^2 < L(7/8)(6241/961), which is about 22.73 for L=4 and 28.41 for L=5, both below 36."},{"severity":"optional (sharpening)","section":"Theorem L2 closing sentence; Section 4 Jensen remark","problem":"For deterministic disturbances, any mean-square-feasible controller is also literally feasible at the same gamma, since N1(z)<=N2(z) and N1(w)=N2(w). So, if the old sufficiency result holds, the Riccati condition is sufficient for the literal problem with deterministic inputs. Only the adapted case is open, which matches the text's caveat.","suggested_fix":"Add this one line to sharpen the sentence 'does not prove or disprove sufficiency ... for arbitrary adapted literal inputs'."},{"severity":"optional (robustness note)","section":"Lemma L1; Section 0","problem":"Two robustness facts are not stated. First, L1 and L2.1 need only w(s) to be F_{s+h}-measurable, so they hold whether adaptedness is imposed on w or only on the delayed signal w(t-h). Second, the impossibility in L2.2 uses a deterministic test input, so it does not depend on how preview is modelled.","suggested_fix":"Add a remark recording both facts, to head off objections about the preview convention."},{"severity":"optional","section":"Theorem L2 data","problem":"If the book normalizes D1'D1=I, the example still applies: D1'D0=0 already holds, and the rescaling u~=100u with B=1/100 gives the same system.","suggested_fix":"Optionally mention this rescaling."}],"independent_derivations":[{"topic":"Scalar moments","result":"G(r)=exp((a-sigma^2/2)r+sigma W_r). E G=e^{ar}. E G^2=exp((2a-sigma^2)r+2sigma^2 r)=e^{qr}. For L2: a=-1, sigma=2, q=2, and u=-2x gives 2(-3)+4=-2. For L3: G=exp(W_2-W_1-1/2), so E G=1 and E G^2=e."},{"topic":"Variation of constants","result":"Let Y=Phi(.,0), c(t)=int_0^t Y^{-1} f dr (bounded variation), and x=Yc. Then dx=c dY+Y dc=(ax+f)dt+sigma x dW, and Phi(t,0)/Phi(r,0)=Phi(t,r)."},{"topic":"L1 constants","result":"M<=sum_n e^{a n delta} sqrt(J_q(delta))=H_delta. With a=-1, sigma=2, delta=1: J_2(1)=(e^2-1)/2, about 3.19453; H_1 is about 1.78732/0.63212=2.8275; 2H_1 is about 5.655 and its square about 31.98, below 33.6 and 36. With delta=1/2: H is about 2.3557. The minimum, about 2.3548, occurs near delta=0.48."},{"topic":"Pulse moments (L5)","result":"Ito gives d(x^2)=(2x^2+2x)dt+4x^2 dW on [1,2], so s'=2s+2m and m'=1-m. Hence m=1-e^{-r} and s=e^{2r}/3-1+(2/3)e^{-r}. The Taylor series r^2+r^3/3 matches the ODE. s(1)=e^2/3-1+2/(3e), about 1.708272. On [2,5], s'=2s. D=s(1)(e^6-1)/2, about 343.729. The exact value is N2(d)^2=D+e^2/6-1/2-2/(3e), about 344.215."},{"topic":"Hilbert operator bound","result":"For u(s) F_s-measurable, the squared L2(Omega x time) norm of 1{t>=s}Phi(t,s)u(s) is E[u(s)^2] J_q(T-s). Minkowski followed by Cauchy-Schwarz gives N2(Su)^2<=N2(u)^2 int_0^T J_q, which equals (e^{qT}-1-qT)/q^2, or T^2/2 when q=0. For q=2 and T=5: M_5^2=(e^10-11)/4, about 5503.87, and M_5^2/1e4 is about 0.550387."},{"topic":"(L6)","result":"ratio^2>=D/(1+M_5^2/1e4), about 343.729/1.550387=221.705, so the bound is about 14.890. Rigorously, with 2.7<e<2.72 and monotonicity, ratio^2>208.5>196, so the bound exceeds 14.43."},{"topic":"L3 values","result":"|z|^2=2(u+dx/2)^2+(dx)^2/2, and x=GX+V on [3,4]. Literal: E|GX+V|<=E|X|+E|V|<=sqrt2 E sqrt(X^2+V^2)<=sqrt2 N1(w), with equality at X=V=1, so the gain is 1. Adapted mean-square: ||GX+V||<=sqrt(e)U+V2<=sqrt(e+1)sqrt(U^2+V2^2). With X=1 and V=G/e, GX and V are positively collinear and U:V2=sqrt(e):1, giving gain sqrt((e+1)/2), about 1.3635. Deterministic mean-square: the quadratic form is eX^2+2XV+V^2 with lambda_max=(e+1+sqrt((e-1)^2+4))/2, about 3.1775, so the gain is about 1.2605."},{"topic":"Information/integrability audit","result":"L1 uses only w(s) in F_{s+h} and N1(w) finite. L2.2 uses only u(s) in F_s, plus a deterministic L2 input that is admissible in every class. L3 uses X in F_1 and allows V to depend on G. No step assumes N2(w) finite where only N1(w) finite is given, and no supremum over deterministic inputs is swapped for one over adapted inputs."}],"scope_verdict":"Within scope and accurately labelled. L1, the Hilbert estimate, L2 and L3 are mathematically correct, and no load-bearing defect was found. Two fixes are required, both minor: give an in-text rational certificate for (L6), which is true (rigorously above 14.43, about 14.89 exactly), and state that the Riccati-necessity corollary depends on unpinned old theorems. Finite and infinite horizons are kept apart, and so are deterministic and adapted disturbances; L3 even exhibits different deterministic and adapted mean-square optima. L2 is a genuine all-controller existence separation at gamma=6. L3 proves both necessity and sufficiency (gamma>1) for one gated plant, by a pathwise argument that is valid because the state does not depend on the control; it does not address preview or actuation. Nothing in the file claims a partial theorem solves the general book problem, though 'subclass' slightly overstates L3. Planned numerical checks were not treated as evidence; (L4) and (L6) were checked by hand."}
